outputs.exact_statement: Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective complex manifold of dimension at least two. Suppose that two general points of $X$ lie on the image of a morphism $\mathbb P^1\to X$. For every specified holomorphic decomposition $$T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$$ into subbundles of positive rank, both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are integrable.
Under the hypotheses of 1, there are smooth projective manifolds $X_1,X_2$ and an isomorphism $X\simeq X_1\times X_2$ under which $$E_i=\operatorname{pr}_i^*T_{X_i}\qquad (i=1,2).$$

Every holomorphic map $g:C\to X$ admits a holomorphic map $F:S\to X$ such that $$\label{eq:box}
F|_\Delta=g,\qquad
dF(T^{(1)})\subset F^*E_1,\qquad
dF(T^{(2)})\subset F^*E_2.$$ Neither summand is assumed integrable.
There is a unique formal holomorphic map $\widehat F$ along $\Delta$ with diagonal value $g$ and the two tangency properties in [eq:box], interpreted formally.

Let $Y\subset\mathbb P^N$ be a closed complex submanifold and let $\widehat G$ be a formal holomorphic map from the formal neighborhood of $\Delta\subset S$ to $Y$. There is a rational map $R:S\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^N$ that is holomorphic on a neighborhood of a nonempty open subset of $\Delta$, where its formal expansion agrees with $\widehat G$. On that neighborhood it takes values in $Y$.

Let $R:S\dashrightarrow X$ be a rational map such that, on its domain of definition, $$dR(T^{(1)})\subset R^*E_1,\qquad
dR(T^{(2)})\subset R^*E_2.$$ Then $R$ extends to a holomorphic map $S\to X$.

Fix distinct $a,b\in C$. There are a nonempty complex manifold $T$ and a holomorphic map $G:C\times T\to X$ such that $$(\operatorname{ev}_a,\operatorname{ev}_b):T\longrightarrow X\times X,\qquad
\tau\longmapsto (G(a,\tau),G(b,\tau))$$ is a submersion. In particular, for $g=G(\,\cdot\,,\tau)$, the global sections of $g^*E_i$ vanishing at $a$ have values spanning $E_i$ at $g(b)$.

Let $X$ be a connected uniruled compact Kähler manifold with a holomorphic splitting $T_X=V_1\oplus V_2$. Let $Z$ be a general fiber of its rationally connected quotient and set $W_i=T_Z\cap V_i|_Z$. For each $i=1,2$, there is an almost-holomorphic fibration $\phi_i:X\dashrightarrow Y_i$ whose general fiber $F_i$ is rationally connected and, for compatible choices $F_i\subset Z$, satisfies $$T_{F_i}=W_i|_{F_i}\subset V_i|_{F_i}.$$ If $W_i=0$, one may take $\phi_i=\operatorname{id}_X$, with point fibers.*

*If $\operatorname{rank}V_1=2$, exactly one of the following holds:*

1.  *$W_1=V_1|_Z$, and $X$ admits an analytic fiber bundle $X\to Y$ with rationally connected general fiber and $T_{X/Y}=V_1$.*

2.  *$W_1$ is a line bundle, and there is an equidimensional holomorphic map $X\to Y$ whose general fiber $F$ is a rational curve with $T_F\subset V_1|_F$.*

3.  *$W_1=0$, equivalently $T_Z\subset V_2|_Z$.

A rational map $R:\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^N$ is holomorphic outside a finite set $B$. A finite sequence of point blowups over $B$ gives a smooth projective surface $\mu:S'\to\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ on which $R\circ\mu$ extends holomorphically. The fibers of $\mu$ are connected; its exceptional components are smooth curves.
